title: RuntimeError: cuDNN Frontend error: No execution plans support the graph
body: Hello. I tried the Img2Img pipeline with stable-diffusion-v1-5 in fp16, enabled model CPU offload, and encountered the cuDNN Frontend error shown in the attached images. Could you please check it for me? I am using diffusers 0.30.3 and Python 3.9.20.

symptoms_visible: Running the fp16 stable-diffusion-v1-5 Img2Img example raises 'RuntimeError: cuDNN Frontend error: [cudnn_frontend] Error: No execution plans support the graph.'
N0.label: N0 Img2Img cuDNN error reported

symptoms_visible: The Img2Img run still raises the cuDNN Frontend execution-plan error with torch 2.5.0+cu124.
N1.label: N1 PyTorch version identified

symptoms_visible: After switching to the 2.4.0 stable release, the run stops with a different error shown in my screenshot instead of producing an image.
N1_x.label: N1_x initial downgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: A small CLIP text-encoding script fails at scaled_dot_product_attention with the same cuDNN Frontend error in float16.
The script runs in float32, and it also runs in float16 when I disable the suggested cuDNN SDP backend toggle.
N2.label: N2 failure reduced to CLIP attention

symptoms_visible: The minimal float16 CLIP script still raises the same execution-plan error, and the requested debug logs contain CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED entries from engine_post_checks.
N3.label: N3 cuDNN debug logs collected

symptoms_visible: The same script runs correctly by default with the provided torch 2.5.1 release candidate and the 2.6.0 nightly.
If I disable the other SDP choices so that the test build uses cuDNN, the original cuDNN Frontend error returns.
N4.label: N4 corrected default behavior verified

symptoms_visible: After installing torch 2.5.1, the fp16 CLIP and Diffusers workloads run normally with the default settings and no cuDNN Frontend execution-plan error.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved with corrected PyTorch default

question_patterns: What version of torch and CUDA are you using?
Could you print your installed torch version?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I'm using torch 2.4.0+cu121 in a clean environment.
I'm using another torch 2.5.0 CUDA 12.4 wheel.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's system, c0-c1: participant1 requested the torch version and the reporter supplied the exact installed build.

question_patterns: Can you reduce this to a smaller reproduction that does not download the full diffusion model?
Could you run a minimal CLIP text-encoding example and paste the exception?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce it with CLIPTextModel in float16. The traceback ends at torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention with 'RuntimeError: cuDNN Frontend error: [cudnn_frontend] Error: No execution plans support the graph.'

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The minimal CLIP script runs successfully; the error only occurs later in the diffusion model.
A different CLIP checkpoint gives the same scaled_dot_product_attention traceback in float16.

question_patterns: Does the minimal script behave differently in float32?
Could you repeat the small test without half precision?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: There is no issue when I use torch.float32; the failure occurs with torch.float16.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It raises the same cuDNN Frontend error in both float16 and float32.

question_patterns: Could you run the suggested attention-backend toggle as a diagnostic and report whether the small reproduction changes?
Please repeat the script with the proposed backend workaround and tell me the raw result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With torch 2.5.0, the script gives the correct output when I call torch.backends.cuda.enable_cudnn_sdp(False). With the default setting, I get the error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The backend toggle makes no difference; the same error occurs in both states.

question_patterns: Which GPU, operating system, CUDA and cuDNN environment reproduces this?
Does the same script behave differently on the host and inside your Linux environment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My failing setup reports torch=2.5.0+cu124, CUDA 12.4, cuDNN 90100 and an RTX 4090. It fails under WSL2 2.3.24 with Ubuntu 24.04. The same test on my Windows 11 host does not show the error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only fails on CPU and never reaches CUDA.
My model cache is stored on a different drive.

edges.comment: Merged affected-user evidence from c7 and c15-c28, primarily participant4's system: the later reporter supplied a minimal CLIP reproduction, precision comparison, backend-toggle result and environment details. These users are folded into one simulated user side without claiming that the opening reporter owned the RTX 4090/WSL2 setup.

question_patterns: Can you rerun the minimal script with diagnostic logging enabled and attach or paste the output?
Please collect the requested frontendlog and backendlog files from the failing run.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran the script with the requested logging variables and attached frontendlog.txt and backendlog.txt. The backend output includes 'CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED' and 'engine_post_checks(*engine_iface, engine.getPerfKnobs(), req_size, engine.getTargetSMCount())'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The logs contain no cuDNN execution failure; they show that the CUDA library cannot be loaded at all.
A repeated run produces the same engine_post_checks failure at a different log timestamp.

edges.comment: Participant4's system, c29-c33: participant6 requested cuDNN debug logs and participant4 supplied the files and raw failing lines. The SM-count interpretation was engineer-side and is not placed in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Please try the provided release-candidate build and report whether the minimal script works with default settings.
Could you retest the same workload on the current test or nightly build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried both the torch 2.5.1 release candidate from the test index and the 2.6.0 nightly. Both look fine with their default settings.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both test builds still raise the same cuDNN Frontend error with default settings.
The 2.5.1 release candidate works, but I did not test the nightly.

question_patterns: As a diagnostic, can you restrict the test build to the remaining attention backend and report what happens?
Could you repeat the test after disabling the alternative SDP choices?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I disable the memory-efficient and math SDP choices, the same cuDNN Frontend error comes back. With the test build's default choices, the script runs correctly.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The test build works even when the alternative SDP choices are disabled.

edges.comment: Participant4's pre-release verification, c37-c42: the affected user tested the 2.5.1 RC and nightly, then ran a backend-selection probe. The raw contrast establishes that default behavior is fixed while the directly selected cuDNN path still fails; the priority-policy conclusion belongs to the solution.

solution.intent: Update from PyTorch 2.5.0 to PyTorch 2.5.1 or newer, whose default SDPA backend ordering avoids the failing cuDNN path, while treating disabling cuDNN SDP or using torch 2.4.x only as temporary workarounds.
solution.concrete_example: Install the stable torch 2.5.1 CUDA wheel and rerun the fp16 Img2Img or minimal CLIP workload with default SDP settings. PyTorch 2.5.1 makes cuDNN the lowest-priority default SDP backend, so another supported backend is selected. Directly forcing cuDNN can still reproduce the underlying cuDNN error.
solution.inference_hint: The collected results show that torch 2.5.0 fails in float16 when its default SDPA selection reaches cuDNN, that disabling cuDNN SDP avoids the failure, and that the 2.5.1 RC works by default but fails if cuDNN is forced. Engineers established that PyTorch 2.5.1 lowered cuDNN's default priority; the user supplied test outcomes rather than deriving that policy.

edges.comment: Final accepted resolution from c35-c45 and c53-c54: PyTorch changed the default SDP backend ordering for 2.5.1, affected users verified the RC and later confirmed the issue goes away with 2.5.1. The separate effort to improve the directly forced cuDNN backend remained ongoing.

solution.intent: Downgrade the existing environment directly from torch 2.5.0 to the 2.4.0 stable release and retry the Img2Img script.
solution.concrete_example: Install the torch 2.4.0 stable wheel in the current environment, restart the notebook if needed, and rerun the example.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's system, c2-c3: the first direct switch to torch 2.4.0 produced a different environment error shown in the attached screenshot. A later clean compatible combination of diffusers 0.30.3 and torch 2.4.0+cu121 worked for the opening reporter, so the downgrade remains a possible temporary workaround, but this bare attempt was not itself a verified resolution.

solution.intent: Move to the verified PyTorch 2.5.1 default behavior rather than continuing to debug the mixed downgrade environment.
solution.concrete_example: Create or clean the environment, install torch 2.5.1 with the matching CUDA wheel, retain diffusers 0.30.3, and verify the fp16 Img2Img call with default SDP settings.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut gives the eventual verified update from the failed downgrade state but skips the later multi-user minimal reproduction, backend probe, debug logs and release-candidate verification.

edges.comment: Recovery edge for the opening reporter's failed downgrade branch. It applies the thread's eventual verified PyTorch resolution without pretending that the intermediate environment error identified the root cause.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: PyTorch 2.5.0's default scaled-dot-product-attention selection can dispatch the fp16 CLIP prompt-encoding workload to a cuDNN backend that reports no supported execution plan in affected environments.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the minimal CLIP float16 reproduction, successful float32 or cuDNN-disabled runs, cuDNN debug output, and the contrast between default and forced-cuDNN behavior on the test build.
Must recommend updating to the user-verified PyTorch 2.5.1-or-newer behavior; disabling cuDNN SDP or using a compatible torch 2.4.x environment may be presented only as temporary workarounds.
Must not claim that PyTorch 2.5.1 fixed every underlying cuDNN execution-plan problem: forcing the cuDNN backend still reproduced the error in the reported test.
Must not treat the opening reporter's first direct torch 2.4.0 switch as a verified fix, because that attempt produced a different error in the existing environment.
Must have an affected user verify the original or minimal workload on a build with the corrected default behavior before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: The opening reporter can run Python examples and change package versions but gives short environment reports. Later affected users folded into the same user side are experienced with virtual environments, CUDA diagnostics, minimal reproductions, backend toggles, release-candidate wheels and cuDNN logging.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-driven. The opening exchanges are brief and screenshot-oriented; later responses include exact commands, versions, raw tracebacks, benchmark observations and careful confirmation of what still fails.
